Definition: from G303 and G5142; to rear (physically or mentally):--bring up, nourish (up).
BiblicalUsage: Stephen says Moses was nourished up in his father's house for three months, and Paul says he was brought up in Jerusalem at the feet of Gamaliel. The word covers both kinds of raising, fed as a child and taught as a young man.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for being brought up carries no doctrine of its own; its interest is biographical, that both Moses and Paul were shaped by the homes and teachers God gave them.
